faq.title: Common questions
faq.a1: Stress testing infrastructure you own — or have written authorization to test — is legal in most jurisdictions. SupremeBot is built for that use, and is not intended for use against infrastructure you do not control.
faq.a2: Hosts and services you operate, or infrastructure where you hold written authorization to load-test. If you are unsure whether a target is in scope, confirm with its owner before launching.
faq.q3: What is the difference between Layer 4 and Layer 7?
faq.a3: Layer 4 operates at the transport layer (TCP, UDP) and measures raw throughput and connection-table saturation. Layer 7 operates at the application layer and measures how your web stack handles realistic traffic at scale.
faq.q4: Does the platform have an API?
faq.a4: Yes. Launch, stop, list and inspect tests via single HTTP calls — GET and POST, JSON over TLS. API keys are scoped, rotatable and revocable.
faq.a5: About 60 seconds. Sign up, choose a plan and run your first test. Most users launch within five minutes.
faq.a6: Yes. All plans are month-to-month with no long-term contracts. Upgrade, downgrade or cancel from the billing panel at any time.

security.title: Account security by default
security.subtitle: The controls that keep a testing account from becoming a liability — on by default, not sold as an upgrade.
security.identityDesc: Two-factor authentication on every account, with email alerts for new sign-ins and unrecognised devices.
security.apiDesc: Scoped API keys you can rotate and revoke, with optional IP allowlisting so a leaked key is useless from anywhere else.
security.alertsDesc: Sign-in history, active sessions and security events are retained and exportable — activity on your account is always accountable.
security.teamDesc: Invite teammates with role-based permissions, so nobody gets the ability to launch a test unless they need it.

tools.title: Free reconnaissance tools
tools.subtitle: Enumerate and inspect infrastructure you own or are authorised to assess — certificate transparency, host reachability and response headers. No signup, no key, no log retained on our side.
tools.scopeNote: Probe only hosts you own or have written permission to assess. Requests are not logged.
tools.errorHost: Enter a valid hostname, e.g. example.com
tools.errorGeneric: Lookup failed. Try again in a moment.
tools.empty: Enter a host above to enumerate its certificate footprint or inspect its response headers.
tools.noneFound: No certificates found for this domain.
tools.nxdomain: {{host}} does not resolve — the name is not registered or has no DNS records.
tools.noRecords: No records returned for this query.
tools.cdnHintLabel: Fronted by a CDN or WAF.
tools.cdnHintNote: Observed from reverse DNS only. The reported address belongs to the front, not to anything behind it.
tools.dashSubtitle: Enumerate and inspect infrastructure you own or are authorised to assess — certificate transparency, DNS resolution and response headers. No signup, no key.
tools.dashNote: Every lookup goes through the scoped bridge: the tool name selects the upstream from a fixed list and only a hostname leaves your browser, so this panel cannot be aimed at an arbitrary URL.

services.title: Work done by our team, not just tooling
services.subtitle: Some questions need a person reading the output, not a form. These are delivered manually by our team, scoped to infrastructure you own or are authorised to have assessed.
services.originHeadline: Find the real origin behind Cloudflare, DDoS-Guard and similar fronts
services.originDesc: When a CDN or mitigation front answers for a name you are authorised to assess, we trace it back to its authoritative origin through passive sources — certificates, history, and the name's own configuration — and hand you a written report.
services.originB1: Written report of the identified origin and the chain of evidence
services.originB2: Passive sources only — no traffic is sent at your host
services.originB3: Turnaround within 48 hours, scoped to the domains you own
services.originStaticNote: Static HTML sites with no separate origin cannot be traced this way — there is nothing behind the front to find. If that turns out to be the case we tell you and refund the order.
services.originScopeNote: We take this on for infrastructure you own or have written authorisation to assess. Requests against third parties are refused.
services.originLegal: Delivery is handled by a person, not an automated form.
